quote: we generate abstractive summaries whilst controlling their length and the extent to which the query influences their content.
... we proposed an abstractive framework for query focused summarization ...

We further decompose abstractive QFS into two subtasks: (1) query modeling (i.e., finding supportive evidence within a set of documents for a query) and (2) conditional language modeling (i.e., generating an abstractive summary based on found evidence).
We use ROUGE F1 to evaluate the resulting summaries so that precision is also taken into account.

We use ROUGE as a distant supervision signal, and train a model that takes a query and document sentence as input and estimates their relevance.

We also evaluated model summaries in a judgment elicitation study via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Native English speakers (self-reported) were asked to rate query-summary pairs on two dimensions: Succinctness (does the summary avoid unnecessary detail and redundant information?) and Coherence (does the summary make logical sense?).
guideline: Participants were asked to rate query-summary pairs on Succinctness and Coherence using a five-point Likert scale, and assess Relevance by scoring sentences as relevant, partially relevant, or irrelevant.
Rate each summary on Succinctness, Coherence, and Relevance using a five-point Likert scale; also score sentence relevance (5, 2.5, 0).

Participants were asked to rate query-summary pairs on two dimensions: Succinctness and Coherence using a five-point Likert scale. For Relevance assessment, participants decided whether each sentence was relevant (score 5), partially relevant (score 2.5), or irrelevant (score 0).
